-83.30680,42.50180.name: Wayne Health
-83.30680,42.50180.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

120.30072,22.67782.name: Fertility clinic (unnamed in OpenStreetMap)
120.30072,22.67782.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-71.15228,42.47926.name: Cephrim Biosciences
-71.15228,42.47926.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.14840,51.51722.name: Aria Fertility
-0.14840,51.51722.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-2.30207,53.59345.name: CREATE Fertility Bury
-2.30207,53.59345.state: Hilton House, Irwell Street, Greater Manchester, Bury, BL9 0HZ
-2.30207,53.59345.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Manchester
-2.30207,53.59345.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Manchester. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-70.56332,-33.39452.name: SGFertility
-70.56332,-33.39452.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.sgfertility.cl. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

127.32700,36.64000.name: Osong BSL-4 Laboratory, Korea Centers for Disease
127.32700,36.64000.state: Osong Health Technology Administration Complex, 187, Osongsaengmyeong , Republic of Korea
127.32700,36.64000.company: Korean Disease Control and Prevention Agency
127.32700,36.64000.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by Korean Disease Control and Prevention Agency. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 300 SqM. Operational or announced: 2017. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

106.84560,-6.20880.name: PT Perkebunan Nusantara / sugarcane biotechnology
106.84560,-6.20880.desc: Indonesia’s state plantation company, which grew engineered drought-tolerant sugarcane developed domestically — one of the few engineered crops anywhere developed by a public body for a national crop rather than by a multinational for an export commodity.

106.84560,-6.20880.name: Badan POM — Indonesian food and drug authority
106.84560,-6.20880.desc: Indonesia's biosafety commission issues the certificates, and the food and drug authority's Regulation 19 of 2024 set the standards that decide what needs one. The regulation added genome editing explicitly: an edited food is classified either as a GM food derived from genome editing or as a non-GM food, on an assessment by the commission, and only the first needs a food-safety approval certificate. Two classifications, one assessment, and the assessment is not published as a register. In the fourth most populous country on Earth the question of which edited foods are on the market is answered by a certificate file rather than by a list.

-122.48000,47.75000.name: The Non-GMO Project
-122.48000,47.75000.desc: The largest GMO-avoidance certification in North America, verifying tens of thousands of products. A private label doing what a labelling law would do, funded by the companies seeking the label — which means the standard is set by the market for it rather than by a legislature, and it covers only what its members choose to submit. It is also the reason a great deal of American food carries a GMO statement at all.

116.39600,39.90800.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (China) — biosafety certificates
116.39600,39.90800.desc: Issues the biosafety certificates without which no engineered crop may be grown in China, and has used that power as a tap: cotton and papaya approved, food crops held back for over a decade, then maize and soy released from 2019. The clearest case anywhere of approval timing being a policy instrument rather than a technical outcome.
